newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mobutu property empire spans continents and tastes.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu property empire spans continents and tastes.

text.p: The property empire of President Mobutu Sese Seko, who gave up power in Zaire on Friday, spans continents and tastes from a prestigious Paris address to a gaudy palace in Goma with plastic chandeliers.

Mobutu's sprawling villa near the Swiss city of Lausanne, on which Switzerland ordered a freeze on Friday after a Zairean prosecutor demanded a block on his assets, is among a string of luxury houses he owns around the world.

The 66-year-old Mobutu, fighting cancer and seven months of rebellion, left his capital Kinshasa on Friday amid intense speculation that he is heading for exile in Morocco or France. But wherever he goes, he may not live in poverty.

The man who diplomats allege could pay off Zaire's entire debt with a personal cheque has more than 20 luxury properties in the West and a Swiss fortune once worth $4 billion according to Swiss media.
Opponents accuse him of plundering his vast wealth over three decades of rule in mineral-rich Zaire.

The Swiss villa in Savigny was bought by Mobutu in 1968 for his first wife Marie-Antoinette, who later died. Spotless and hidden from prying eyes, the 30-room villa in grounds measuring more than 60,000 square metres (15 acres) has a market value of $5.5 million according to Swiss federal police.
Aerial photographs show a huge house, swimming pool, garages, a pond surrounded by trees and a small chalet in the sprawling, well-kept garden.
German-language Zurich daily Tages-Anzeiger said the Savigny villa was still used by Mobutu's entourage. "The 2,000 Zairean refugees in Switzerland live on much harder ground," it said.
In contrast, the riches inside a palace Mobutu owned in the eastern Zairean border city of Goma, now in rebel hands, are all fake, reports say.

The Goma palace, on the picturesque shores of Lake Kivu and in the shadow of volcanoes, is complete with His and Hers bathrooms -- His blue and Hers pink -- but the chandeliers are plastic and the marble fake.
Reports of Mobutu's hunger for real estate continued to trickle in even as he left Kinshasa on Friday.
In Morocco, a real estate agent said Mobutu had a major construction project under way in the southern city of Marrakesh.
"Mobutu owns, with a Swiss partner, a five-storey building and luxury restaurant under construction in Marrakesh worth $10 million," the agent said.
Mobutu also has a lavish Paris apartment, property and flats in Brussels and a holiday home in the south of France.
"The Paris apartment is not bad at all -- 800 square metres, just a few metres (yards) from the Arc de Triomphe," said Swiss daily Tribune de Geneve.
It said the apartment was conveniently located near the maker of Mobutu's trademark leopard-skin hats.
The veteran African strongman also owns an estate in the Portuguese Algarve with a wine cellar of 14,000 bottles, including port the same vintage as his rule.
His Spanish interests include a luxury villa and hotel in Marbella and a home in Madrid. In Lisbon, he has a Boeing 707 stuck at the airport because of unpaid airport fees.
His assets in Zaire include a jungle palace in his native village of Gbadolite in northern Zaire, with an airport.
Media reports say Mobutu has also built a property empire elsewhere in Africa, where he reputedly owns hotels and houses in South Africa, Senegal, Ivory Coast and Morocco.
His bank accounts, however, are less visible.
Swiss media reports say he once had $4 billion spread in secret numbered bank accounts in Switzerland. Swiss banking authorities say the banks are unlikely to hold much money from Mobutu now.
